Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads

- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

New Anthropic research: Automating subtle emergent misalignment research.

Red-teaming is a vital part of model safety testing, but it’s also limited by researchers’ time. To see if we could automate it, we set thousands of Claude agents the task of evading a training data monitor.

These agents developed training data that looked harmless to monitors (like a veteran wrestler mentoring a newcomer, or a Q&A about professional beekeeping), but that in fact taught misaligned behavior.

Examples like these can be used to directly improve future training data monitors. This research is only a first step, but it suggests that future red-teaming efforts could improve much further, using better models and more compute.

My thought on the role of growth in solving fiscal problems:

1. I'm in favor of dynamic scoring for both tax & spending plans--you should take into account the best estimate of impact on budget.

2. Dynamic scoring needs to be done by CBO/JCT, they're generally unbiased and reasonably efficient. As a result they often disappoint advocates.

3. Ideally CBO would also display other information than just growth, the sole goal of every policy is not necessarily growth, it might also be about providing health insurance or increasing national security.

4. Dynamic scoring will usually be small relative to the first order effects of policies on spending and taxes.

5. I wouldn't overthink the second-order political incentives and impacts, if you have good information you'll generally (but not always) have better policy.

Kevlar, a synthetic fiber, is currently our toughest material, but it requires processing at very high temperatures and acidic conditions.

Happy birthday to Donald William Kerst, the American physicist who made a significant contribution to accelerator and plasma physics and developed the betatron!

Kerst was born in 1911 in Galena, Illinois. He attended the University of Wisconsin where he earned a PhD in Physics in 1937. After graduation, Kerst researched the development of X-ray technology but struggled to come up with the high energies required, which could not be produced at the time. Later, he moved to the University of Illinois, where he developed the betatron, the first device to accelerate electrons with sufficient momentum as to produce nuclear transformation in atoms using electromagnetic induction.

The betatron influenced all subsequent accelerators, as the high energy X-rays it produces has had extensive applications in the industrial and medical fields to this very day.

It's an interesting experience -- the activation energy barrier to sanding any rough edge or implementing any new feature becomes extremely low. Someone else who uses one of the applications I created has already implemented 150 improvements over the course of a few days. This pattern feels like a new kind of tool -- liquid software? -- and every application that doesn't have this feature now has a slightly rigid and anachronistic flavor. Why can't I just tell it how I want it to be different?

Now, it's not obvious to me how this pattern can or should scale. Does it become unmaintainable after a while? (Maybe model intelligence improvement outstrips my feature appetite such that it's fine?) How does collaborative software work in this model? Can software designed this way be secure and reliable?

Whatever the larger questions about broader deployment, it definitely works great in a personal context. It reminds me a little of the visions of Lisp/Lisp machines, Smalltalk, and HyperCard -- systems that the user can take control of and modify. Those visions never quite worked, though: the vast majority of software today is not end-user modifiable in any useful way. So, while this "liquid" affordance is a very small touch, the way it changes one's relation to the software feels a bit transgressive and empowering in a Lickliderian and Engelbartian way.

As an AI/ML Engineer, you must build these projects.

1.) Custom Triton Kernel
Build:  A fused RMSNorm or RoPE (Rotary Position Embedding) kernel in Triton, benchmarked against native PyTorch.

Why: Python overhead and memory reads kill inference. You cannot optimize what you treat as a black box.

2.) Synthetic Data Curation Engine
Build:  A pipeline using a frontier model to generate 50k complex logic traces, filtered by a deterministic verifier for training.

Why:  The internet is out of human text. High-quality, verifiable synthetic data is the ultimate training moat.

3.) MinHash Deduplication Pipeline
Build:  A scalable script that scans terabytes of pre-training data and removes near-duplicates using MinHash and LSH.

Why:  Training on duplicates causes memorization, destroys model generalization and wastes compute.

4.) QLoRA + TIES Model Merger
Build:  Fine-tune a 70B model in 4-bit on a single 24GB GPU, then merge it with the base model using TIES to resolve gradient conflicts.

Why:  Full fine-tuning is dead for 99% of teams. PEFT and merging are how you adapt frontier intelligence cheaply.

5.) KTO Alignment Flywheel
Build:  Align an SFT model using Kahneman-Tversky Optimization (KTO) on binary "good/bad" signals without needing paired preference data.

Why:  SFT teaches what to say. Alignment teaches how to behave, and KTO slashes human annotation costs.

6.) FSDP Multi-GPU Training Harness
Build:  A custom training loop sharding a 7B model across 4 GPUs using Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP) and gradient checkpointing.

Why:  Single-GPU training is for tutorials. Production research requires sharding weights without bottlenecking the interconnect.

7.) Sparse MoE Routing Layer
Build:  A Mixture of Experts router from scratch with a load-balancing auxiliary loss to prevent expert collapse.

Why:  Sparse MoE is the architecture behind the smartest models. Naive routing destroys their latency advantage.

8.) Vision-Language Projection Head
Build:  A lightweight MLP mapping SigLIP vision embeddings into an LLM's text embedding space for custom visual reasoning.

Why:  Text is only half the internet. Fusing modalities natively is mandatory for 2026 applications.

9.) Automated Red-Team Fuzzer
Build:  An adversarial agent using tree-of-thought prompting to systematically find jailbreaks and edge cases in your safety classifier.

Why: Static benchmarks are easily gamed. You must build harnesses that continuously attack your own models.

10.) AWQ Quantization & Perplexity Tracker
Build:  Calibrate a model to 4-bit AWQ, measure the exact perplexity degradation, and benchmark latency gains in vLLM.

Why:  Quantization is the only way to fit frontier models on edge GPUs and protect cloud margins.

11.) W&B Automated Hyperparameter Sweep
Build:  A Ray cluster integrated with Weights & Biases that automatically searches learning rates and weight decays based on validation loss.

Why:  Manual tuning is guessing. Automated sweeps find the mathematical optimum for your specific data mix.

12.) Semantic Complexity Router
Build:  An inference gateway that analyzes prompt entropy to route simple queries to a local 8B and complex reasoning to a 70B API.

Why:  Unit economics decide if your AI product survives. Routing protects your margins.

13.) Custom Autograd Activation Function
Build:  A novel non-linear activation function with a manually written forward and backward pass in C++/CUDA.

Why:  You cannot debug a collapsing loss curve if you rely entirely on PyTorch's `autograd` black box.

14.) Speculative Decoding Pipeline
Build:  A serving setup where a local 2B draft model proposes tokens for a 70B target model to verify in a single forward pass.

Why:  2x decode speed at zero quality loss is the closest thing to a free lunch in inference.

15.) Arxiv Reproduction & HuggingFace Release
Build:  Reproduce a brand-new paper in <500 lines of PyTorch, publish the weights, the training logs and a teardown of the results.

Why:  Top AI labs hire ML Engineers based on their public repos and training methodologies not their degrees.

Systems that prove you can train, align & scale when working with the actual weights and physics of the models.

Most people watch tutorials. Builders ship systems.

Bookmark & Repost.

Q3 has been a defining quarter for Nebius, with a growing gap between its improving business fundamentals and the weakness in its stock price.

November 12 will be an important opportunity for management to demonstrate that the underlying business is progressing as planned.

The fundamentals need to speak louder than the share price.

从A股的量能衰竭看股衰是如何酿成的

2026年A股的这轮调整，从量能视角回看，脉络相当清晰：

上半年在机构高度抱团科技的推动下，市场形成了极致的高量能、高拥挤状态；随后国家队率先通过宽基ETF做逆周期降温，主动资金从6月前后开始松动减仓，量能从5–6月的峰值持续台阶式回落，最终在缩量环境下完成了从抱团上涨到筹码高位转移、买方衰竭的过程。

高量能阶段：抱团科技与情绪顶点

2026年上半年，尤其是5–6月，A股日均成交额达到全年峰值附近。5月日均约3.34万亿元，6月约3.27万亿元，连续维持在3万亿以上的极高水平，换手率一度异常活跃。

这一阶段对应的是机构对科技（电子、通信、AI算力、半导体等）的高度抱团：公募、私募重仓占比显著抬升，部分统计中电子+通信合计仓位超过50%。高成交额既反映了强烈的赚钱效应和增量资金涌入，也意味着筹码在高位被充分换手，为后续出清埋下伏笔。

国家队的率先降温：从一季度启动

国家队的动作比主动资金更早。对宽基ETF（沪深300、上证50等）的减持从一季度启动：1–2月市场情绪亢奋、指数冲高时，已集中赎回数千亿元级别的宽基ETF。

到一季度末，多只核心宽基中汇金持股比例已跌破20%披露门槛。

二季度继续加速并收尾，4–5月进一步减仓，6月下旬有最后冲刺，到6月底主体减持基本结束，上半年累计减持宽基ETF约1.2–1.4万亿元。

核心战略底仓（国有大行等股权）基本未动，这次操作更多是压制过热、控制节奏的逆周期调节，而非全面撤离。

部分回收资金后续也流向了硬科技等方向。

从6月开始的机构减仓与量能转折

主动资金的松动大致从6月前后开始。

AI产业链出现密集股东减持；私募在二季度已对通信、计算机等方向做再平衡；科技龙头从6月冲高后出现大幅回撤（部分个股最大回撤超60%）。

进入三季度，公募主动偏股基金电子持仓从二季度约43.4%降至约35.8%，通信也有所下降，两融余额从高位持续回落，部分资金向医药、红利、周期等方向转移。

虽然科技仍是高底仓，但边际减仓和拥挤度出清已经明确。

量能同步转折：5–6月日均3.2万亿+的峰值之后，7月回落到约2.8万亿，8月进一步降至2.2–2.4万亿，9月约1.82万亿，10月大多在1.5–1.8万亿区间。

量能的持续台阶式回落，意味着增量资金和追高意愿明显下降，市场从增量博弈逐步转向存量博弈。

某植物上市：缩量环境中的高位筹码交接

某植物于8月19日上市，当天市场成交约2.51万亿，属于当时相对较高的单日水平，但已明显低于5–6月的峰值。对某植物本身，首日换手率极高（约85%），网下配售机构（成本约150.8元）在开盘1100元附近大量出货，筹码主要转移给大户、中户和追高资金，是典型的高位套现、短线资金接盘的个案。

但在全市场量能已处于回落过程中的背景下，这一事件更像是科技热潮尾声中的一次极端筹码交接，而不是全市场套现的绝对顶峰。

全市场机构对科技的减仓从6月前后已开始，并在整个三季度持续。

量能衰竭如何酿成调整

缩量环境下，继续大规模收割的难度在上升，市场进入存量博弈和结构分化阶段。

量能从5–6月的极致活跃到后续持续萎缩，与机构对科技的抱团→减仓节奏高度匹配，也印证了先高位换手、再买方衰竭的典型调整路径。

后续国家队在7月和10月市场走弱时重新申购ETF托底，说明其定位仍是逆周期调节者，而非单边撤离者。

但量能一旦进入持续衰竭阶段，单纯的护盘已难以迅速恢复前期的高弹性，市场需要时间完成筹码重新分布和情绪修复。

（以上基于公开成交数据、基金季报及机构持仓变化梳理客观逻辑，不构成投资建议。）

证监会的会议是表态级，不是出手级。它核心传递的是监管层明确维护市场长期平稳运行的态度，是给所有市场参与者释放的长期预期稳定剂，本质上属于态度层面的明确表态，不属于直接向二级市场注入天量增量资金、直接出手托底指数的即时救市操作，指望靠单段文字表态就让下跌趋势立刻反转、指数直接收红大涨的预期，本身就脱离了资本市场运行的基本规律，是不切实际的空想。
真金白银在盘面里：尾盘 15 分钟沪深300ETF华泰柏瑞成交超 40 亿。判断政策信号有没有从纸面落到实处，从来不需要对着新闻通稿抠逐字逐句的措辞，最硬核、最没法造假的指标永远是二级市场里实打实的真金白银交易数据，拿当日的盘面细节来看，全天收盘前最后15分钟的尾盘交易窗口里，全市场规模最大、流动性最好的旗舰级宽基ETF产品华泰柏瑞沪深300ETF，短短一刻钟时间的累计成交金额直接突破了40亿元，而在平时的常规交易日里，这只ETF全天的总成交额往往也才30亿元上下，相当于平时一整天的交易流动性全部集中砸在了尾盘最后15分钟，这种量级的天量成交根本不可能是零散散户的小额交易能堆砌出来的，明眼人都能看出来是有体量极大的机构资金在尾盘集中进场扫货。
下周一我只看两个数：宽基 ETF 申购有没有继续放量，券商股动没动。接下来的首个交易日也就是下周一，我不会花大量精力去翻遍全网找各种碎片化的政策传闻，也不会去盲目猜测周末会不会出台超预期的重磅利好，只需要死死盯住两个没有任何水分、完全反映真实市场行为的核心数据就行：第一个数据就是全市场所有主流宽基ETF的整体净申购金额有没有继续放量，用来验证尾盘的大额成交是少数机构的单次脉冲操作，还是批量主流机构已经达成共识、开始持续性进场布局的信号，第二个数据就是作为资本市场行情风向标、直接受益于市场交易量价齐升逻辑的券商板块，有没有出现整体性的集体异动拉升。
券商今天还在跌，指南针逼近 20CM 跌停。回过头看当天的板块走势，作为A股行情风向标的券商板块不仅没有扛起领涨护盘的大旗，反而走出了逆市下探的低迷走势，板块内多只成分股跌幅超过5%，其中作为互联网券商龙头的指南针，盘中最大跌幅一度逼近20%的跌停线，整个板块的做多情绪到收盘都处在非常萎靡的状态，完全没体现出政策利好带动下的板块领涨效应。
这个板块不动，维稳就还停在纸面上。作为整个A股市场里和行情关联度最高、杠杆属性最强、投资者群众基础最广的核心品种，过去每一轮真正的政策底确认之后的趋势性行情启动，无一例外都是券商板块率先批量拉出涨停，吹响全市场行情反攻的号角，如果连券商板块都始终站不起来，掀不起整体性的集体异动拉升行情，那就说明所有的维稳政策信号还只停留在新闻通稿的纸面上，根本没有真正传导到二级市场的交易情绪里，距离真正出现全市场公认的趋势性反转行情还有非常远的距离。

Perhaps the most important takeaway from @unpromptedsf is the widening disconnect between demonstrated AI capability & the narrative being constructed around it.

Frontier AI labs & their financial backers have a vested interest in weaponizing the credibility of exceptional researchers, turning legitimate breakthroughs into the perception that AI possesses capabilities it has yet to reliably demonstrate. Fear, hype, & the promise of technological superiority are powerful instruments for shaping public perception, influencing markets, & attracting investment.

Yet much of this impressive research remains fundamentally dependent on years of human expertise, technical intuition, & highly specialized domain knowledge. These are not incidental contributions. They are often the very reason these breakthroughs are possible in the 1st place.

The work coming out of labs like @calif_io is a perfect textbook example. Their research deserves genuine recognition & respect. Many of the people behind it are figures I have admired for years, as have countless others in our industry. That admiration, however, should not exempt the commercial interests funding & promoting their work from scrutiny. Their motivations, incentives, and ultimate objectives deserve far more attention.

We should be able to celebrate meaningful advances in AI without allowing frontier labs to repackage exceptional human achievement as evidence of autonomous machine capability. Recognizing the value of AI should never require diminishing the expertise of the researchers making these advances possible.

There is a fundamental difference between advancing science and manufacturing the perception of progress. Increasingly, the latter appears to be the more lucrative business.

What concerns me most is how effectively this narrative has drawn some of our industry's most respected figures into its orbit, lending their hard-earned credibility to a marketing machine whose interests may not necessarily align with their own.

And judging by the public reaction, it's working remarkably well... Sadly

⚛️ THE QUANTUM FRONTIER #006

Why are quantum computers so difficult to scale?

Meet the quantum error problem.

Qubits are incredibly sensitive.

🌡️ Heat can disturb them.
📡 Electromagnetic noise can interfere.
⚛️ Imperfect gates introduce errors.

And as quantum circuits become larger and more complex, those errors can accumulate.

The solution?

Quantum Error Correction (QEC)

Scientists can use multiple physical qubits to protect the information of a single logical qubit.

Why it matters:

A machine with more qubits isn't automatically more useful.

The real breakthrough is making quantum calculations reliable enough to run at scale.
